Having your head bitten by the lion is said to bring good health, and children can be seen approaching the lion and shrieking with delight.
quiz_en: In the lion dance, what blessing is it said you receive when the lion bites your head?

desc_en: This shrine stands along the Kiiji route of the Kumano Kodo and is said to be the site of Fujishiro Oji, one of the five highest-ranking of the many Kumano Oji subsidiary shrines. It is regarded as the birthplace of the Suzuki family name nationwide, and the Suzuki residence remains in the grounds. It is also known as a place connected to Prince Arima, a tragic prince of the Asuka period, conveying the history and stories of the Kumano pilgrimage.
quiz_en: Fujishiro Shrine is said to be the birthplace of one of Japan's most common family names. Which name is it?

desc_en: This historic temple in the mountains of Shimotsu-cho, Kainan, is known as the family temple of the Kishu Tokugawa clan. Its main hall, Tahoto pagoda, and great gate, built between the Kamakura and Nanboku-cho periods, are all designated National Treasures, and it is rare for so many National Treasure buildings to survive at one temple. The hill behind holds the graves of successive domain lords, wrapped in a solemn atmosphere.
quiz_en: In the Edo period, Choho-ji became the family temple of which branch of the three main Tokugawa houses?

desc_en: This park on the hills of Kainan is a place where children can run around and play to their hearts' content. With large play equipment and a wide lawn, it bustles with families on weekends and holidays. From the heights you can see the townscape of Kainan and the sea, making it perfect for picnics and walks. You can spend a carefree day here while admiring the seasonal flowers.
quiz_en: If you could become a child again at Wanpaku Park, which piece of play equipment would you most want to try?

desc_en: This garden by the sea in Kainan was created from the Taisho era to the early Showa era. Centered on a pond that draws in seawater, it features sukiya-style buildings and tea rooms, and the garden is designated a national Place of Scenic Beauty. You can take your time savoring the beautiful harmony of the pond, which changes with the tides, the green of the pines, and the buildings.
quiz_en: The water level of the pond at Onzanso Garden changes with the tides because the pond takes in what?

desc_en: This festival is held in Arida, a city known for growing mandarin oranges. Its name comes from Kinokuniya Bunzaemon, a wealthy merchant said to have made his fortune in the Edo period by shipping Kishu mandarins to Edo. During the festival, dances and parades brighten the town, and local people come together to celebrate. You can enjoy the cheerful, lively atmosphere of this home of Arida mandarins.
quiz_en: Who was the merchant, said to have made his fortune from Kishu mandarins, after whom the Kibun Festival is named?

desc_en: This is the annual autumn festival of Obata Hachiman Shrine in Gobo, a major event involving the whole town. Yotsu-daiko drum floats, lion dances, and banners set out from each district, and the town bustles all day long. Above all, the "Suzume Odori," in which children dress as sparrows and dance, is the traditional performing art that symbolizes the festival. It is a festival the locals are proud of, filling the town of Gobo with excitement and smiles.
quiz_en: What is the name of the dance performed at the Gobo Festival that imitates the lightly hopping movements of a bird?

desc_en: This is the head shrine of the thousands of Kumano shrines across Japan and one of the three grand shrines of Kumano. It is part of the World Heritage Site "Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range" and welcomes pilgrims who arrive on foot along the Kumano Kodo. At Oyunohara, a sandbar in the Kumano River where the shrine once stood, rises one of Japan's largest torii gates, and talismans and a mailbox feature Yatagarasu, regarded as a messenger of the gods.
quiz_en: What is the name of the three-legged crow regarded as a messenger of the gods at Kumano Hongu Taisha?

name_en: Tsuboyu and Yuzutsu of Yunomine Onsen
desc_en: Yunomine Onsen, in a valley near Kumano Hongu Taisha, is said to be one of the oldest hot springs in Japan. Tsuboyu, inside a small hut on the riverbank, is said to change color several times a day and is known as a hot spring registered as part of a World Heritage Site. At the Yuzutsu by the river, you can enjoy "yuzutsu cooking," boiling eggs and vegetables in the scalding spring water that gushes out.
quiz_en: What is the name of the small rock bath at Yunomine Onsen that is registered as part of a World Heritage Site?

desc_en: This park is located in Akitsugawa, Tanabe, the home of high-quality Kishu binchotan charcoal. It has an exhibition facility introducing the history and production methods of binchotan, and you can tour a charcoal kiln and try charcoal making yourself. Kishu binchotan, made by firing ubame oak at high temperatures, is prized by chefs because it is hard and burns for a long time. In the quiet air of the mountain village, you can encounter charcoal culture.
quiz_en: What hard, sturdy type of tree is mainly used as the raw material for making Kishu binchotan charcoal?

desc_en: This temple stands on a hill overlooking central Tanabe. Its grounds hold the grave of the naturalist Kumagusu Minakata, who spent the latter half of his life in Tanabe, and many people come to visit it. Morihei Ueshiba, the founder of aikido, was also from Tanabe, and his grave is at this temple too. Looking out over the Aizu River and the townscape of Tanabe, it is a place to reflect on the great figures of the region.
quiz_en: Who is the naturalist with ties to Tanabe, known for research on slime molds, who rests at Kozan-ji Temple?

desc_en: This gorge stretches along the upper reaches of the Migi-Aizu River in Kamiakizu, Tanabe. A clear stream rushes through a valley of piled-up giant rocks, creating a rugged landscape that truly deserves to be called spectacular, as its name suggests. There are also Buddhist images carved into the rock face and small waterfalls, so you can encounter both nature and traces of faith while walking along the gorge. In autumn, colorful leaves adorn the rocks and water, making it even more beautiful.
quiz_en: To see the giant rocks and clear stream of Kizetsukyo Gorge, would you rather visit in fresh green or autumn leaves?

desc_en: This general park spreads across the hills of Tanabe. Equipped with sports facilities, a spacious lawn, and play equipment, it is a place where citizens relax while enjoying sports and picnics. From the heights you can look out over Tanabe Bay and the city, getting a clear sense of Tanabe's landscape surrounded by sea and mountains. It is a pleasant place to get some exercise while admiring the seasonal flowers.
quiz_en: While looking out over Tanabe Bay from the heights of Shinjo General Park, how would you like to spend your time?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) wells up deep in the Kii Mountains along the upper Hidaka River. Together with Yunokawa Onsen in Shimane and Kawanaka Onsen in Gunma, it is counted among Japan's three "hot springs of beauty," and its water is known for its silky feel on the skin. A legend also says it was founded by Kobo Daishi. It is a quiet hot spring town with inns lining the river, where you can soak while viewing the green or autumn colors of the gorge.
quiz_en: Together with Yunokawa Onsen and Kawanaka Onsen, Ryujin Onsen is counted as one of what group of hot springs?

desc_en: This festival, held in Ryujin Village, Tanabe, takes its theme from the village's name, which means "dragon god." Ryujin Village lies in the mountains of the Kii range and is known for the clear Hidaka River, rich forests, and the famous Ryujin Onsen hot spring. On festival day, local people and visitors gather, and amid the warm hospitality unique to a mountain village, you can enjoy a lively time together.
quiz_en: If you took part in the festival in Ryujin Village, which flavors of the mountain village would you like to try?

desc_en: Located in Shingu near the mouth of the Kumano River, this is one of the Kumano Sanzan, the three grand shrines of Kumano. Its vivid vermilion buildings are striking, and the grounds hold a large nagi tree said to have been planted by Taira no Shigemori in the Heian period, designated a national Natural Monument. The deities are said to have been welcomed from Gotobiki-iwa, a giant rock on nearby Mount Kamikura, and every February the spirited Oto Matsuri fire festival is held at Kamikura Shrine.
quiz_en: What kind of tree is the sacred tree in the grounds of Kumano Hayatama Taisha that is designated a national Natural Monument?

desc_en: This gorge runs along the middle reaches of the Kitayama River, a tributary of the Kumano River, continuing upstream from Kumanogawa-cho in Shingu. From upstream, its sections are called Okudoro, Kamidoro, and Shimodoro, and Shimodoro in particular is a scenic spot where tall cliffs close in on both banks and the calm, emerald-colored water flows on. Travel upriver by jet boat, and giant and curious rocks appear one after another as you are wrapped in the mystery of the deep valley.
quiz_en: In Dorokyo Gorge, what is the name of the Shimodoro section, considered especially beautiful, where cliffs close in on both banks?

desc_en: This park in front of Shingu Station is dedicated to Xu Fu, known in Japan as Jofuku. Jofuku is said to have crossed the sea on the orders of Qin Shi Huang, the First Emperor of China, in search of an elixir of immortality, and to have arrived here. A vivid Chinese-style gate catches the eye, and the park contains a monument said to be Jofuku's grave as well as tendai-uyaku trees, regarded as a miraculous medicine.
quiz_en: On the orders of the First Emperor, what kind of elixir granting eternal life is Jofuku said to have searched for?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) is located in the mountains of Kinokawa. Kinokawa is known for producing fruits such as peaches and persimmons, and peaceful orchard scenery spreads across the area. In a quiet setting surrounded by green mountains, you can soak at leisure and soothe your daily fatigue. After bathing, you can enjoy a relaxing time in the Kinokawa countryside while tasting seasonal fruit and local flavors.
quiz_en: After a soak at a hot spring in Kinokawa City, which seasonal fruit would you most like to taste?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) lies at the foot of Mount Ryumon in Kinokawa. Mount Ryumon, called "Kishu Fuji" for its beautiful shape, is popular with hikers. The hot spring is a favorite place to wash off the sweat after a mountain walk, and surrounded by the plains of the Kinokawa River and mountain scenery, you can relax body and mind. Orchards spread around the area, bearing various fruits each season.
quiz_en: Because of its beautiful shape, what nickname is given to Mount Ryumon, which rises near Ryumonzan Onsen?

desc_en: This historic temple in Kokawa, Kinokawa, is the third stop on the Saigoku Thirty-Three Kannon Pilgrimage. It is also known for preserving a National Treasure picture scroll depicting the story of the temple's founding. Its huge main hall is one of the largest among the Saigoku pilgrimage temples, and in front of it lies a garden with magnificent stonework designated a national Place of Scenic Beauty. You can also enjoy the atmosphere of the temple town.
quiz_en: What is the name of the National Treasure picture scroll at Kokawa-dera that depicts the story of the temple's founding?

desc_en: This temple in Kinokawa has long been revered for its Kannon, who protects against misfortune. Many worshippers, including those reaching their yakudoshi (unlucky years), visit to pray for protection, especially at New Year. The temple is surrounded by the gentle farmland and mountains of the Kinokawa River basin, and you can feel the warm atmosphere of Kannon worship carefully preserved by the local community.
quiz_en: At what time of year do especially large numbers of people visit Nagata Kannon to pray for protection from misfortune?

desc_en: This festival brightens summer in Kokawa, Kinokawa, and is the annual rite of Kokawa Ubusuna Shrine, regarded as the guardian shrine of Kokawa-dera. Gorgeous floats set out from each district and parade through the temple town to the music of flutes and drums. It is one of Kishu's leading summer festivals, and the sight of lantern-lit floats moving through the town at night lifts the hearts of all who see it.
quiz_en: What do locals call the decorated floats that parade through the temple town during the Kokawa Festival?

desc_en: This festival, held at Negoro-ji, head temple of the Shingi Shingon school, honors its founder Kogyo Daishi Kakuban. In the Sengoku period Negoro-ji was a major power with its own warrior monks, and its National Treasure Great Pagoda towers over the grounds. During the festival, Buddhist services and events are held, drawing many people to the grounds. The temple is also known for autumn leaves, and you can enjoy strolling around its historic buildings.
quiz_en: The National Treasure Great Pagoda at Negoro-ji is known as a Buddhist pagoda of which architectural type?

desc_en: This prefectural natural park covers the area around Mount Oishigamine, spanning Kimino and Aridagawa towns. Near the summit spreads a grassland of Japanese pampas grass, and in autumn it is covered in silver plumes, making it one of the finest pampas grass spots in Kansai. On clear days you can see as far as the Kii Channel and the mountains of Shikoku, and you can enjoy a refreshing walk amid the grand grassland maintained by controlled burning.
quiz_en: What is the name of the event held in early spring to burn off dead grass in order to preserve the Oishi Kogen grassland?

desc_en: This park on a hill in Katsuragi Town is a famous cherry-blossom viewing spot, with the grounds wrapped in blossoms in spring. Below, the Kinokawa River flows gently, and you can take in the mountains on the far bank and the townscape dotted with persimmon orchards. Katsuragi is known for growing fruits such as persimmons and peaches, and the view from the park reveals the landscape of a bountiful countryside.
quiz_en: While looking down on the Kinokawa River from Katsuragi Park, what food or drink would you bring for cherry-blossom viewing?

desc_en: This is the ichinomiya (highest-ranking shrine) of Kii Province, located in a mountaintop basin in Kamiamano, Katsuragi, and a component of the World Heritage Site "Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range." When Kukai founded Mount Koya, the shrine's deity is said to have granted him the land, giving it deep ties to Koyasan. Cross the vermilion arched bridge called Rinkyo to reach the richly colored gate and main sanctuary, wrapped in a divine atmosphere amid mountain village quiet.
quiz_en: What is the name of the vermilion arched bridge with a great curve that spans the entrance to Niutsuhime Shrine?

desc_en: This festival is held in Kudoyama, where Sanada Masayuki and his son Nobushige (Yukimura) lived in confinement after the Battle of Sekigahara. A samurai procession honoring the Sanada family parades through the town, and the participants, clad in red armor, bring the valiant Sanada warriors back to life. The town has many related sites, such as Sanada-an and the Sanada Museum, making it an irresistible day for fans of the Sengoku period.
quiz_en: Familiar from the Sanada Festival's samurai procession, what is the Sanada family crest made up of six coins called?

desc_en: This event in Kudoyama celebrates the season of harvest. Kudoyama is known for growing Fuyu persimmons, and in autumn the orchards on the mountain slopes are colored with orange fruit. Local farm produce and processed goods line the venue, and you can pick up seasonal flavors while chatting with the producers. You can feel the bountiful autumn of this town, which is also a gateway to Mount Koya.
quiz_en: Which fruit, for which Kudoyama Town is known, colors the mountain slopes orange in the autumn?

desc_en: This gorge was carved into the mountains of Kudoyama by the Nyu River, which originates on Mount Koya. The highly transparent stream flows between rocks large and small, with deep pools and rapids appearing one after another. In summer it bustles with people enjoying river play and camping, and in autumn the trees on both banks change color and adorn the gorge. On the way to Mount Koya, it is a place to experience a clear, unspoiled stream.
quiz_en: In the crystal-clear stream of Tamagawa Gorge, what kind of river play or pastime would you like to try in summer?

desc_en: On Mount Koya, the sacred center of Shingon esoteric Buddhism, you can stay at shukubo (temple lodgings) and eat the same shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) as the training monks. Made without meat or fish, using vegetables, beans, and grains, the dishes draw out the natural flavors of the ingredients and have a deep, nourishing taste. Koyasan specialties such as goma-dofu and koya-dofu line the tray, and eating in a quiet temple room feels like an experience that purifies even the heart.
quiz_en: What is the Koyasan specialty, essential to its shojin cuisine, made by kneading together sesame and kudzu starch?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) lies in the mountains of Yuasa, known as the birthplace of a key Japanese seasoning. The town of Yuasa retains an old townscape lined with brewery storehouses and has been selected as a national Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. After learning about the history of brewing on a town walk, rest your body at leisure in the hot spring, and your trip to Kishu will be even more fulfilling.
quiz_en: Which seasoning, essential to Japanese dining tables, is Yuasa Town, home of Ninomaru Onsen, known as the birthplace of?

desc_en: Oishi Kogen, which can also be climbed from the Aridagawa side, is a grassland spreading near the summit of Mount Oishigamine. It is famous for the sight of pampas grass plumes swaying in the autumn wind, and at dusk the whole grassland glows gold. From the summit you can see the mountains of the Arida River basin and, on clear days, as far as the distant sea. At night the air is clear, and it is also popular as a place for stargazing.
quiz_en: After watching the pampas grass fields of Oishi Kogen at dusk, how would you like to spend the night there?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) sits on the banks of the Arida River in Aridagawa. The "Myoe" in its name comes from a renowned Kamakura-period monk who was born in this area. In a quiet riverside setting, you can soak at leisure while viewing the clear stream. The Arida River basin is known for growing mandarin oranges, and orchards spreading across the mountain slopes add color to the journey to the hot spring.
quiz_en: Who was the renowned Kamakura-period monk born in this area, from whom Kanaya Myoekyo Onsen takes its name?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) is located in the mountains of the Shimizu area, along the upper Arida River. In a quiet spot beside the clear river, you can soak while viewing mountain scenery that changes through the seasons. Rich nature remains in the surrounding area, making it a perfect base for river play in summer and leaf viewing in autumn. Spending relaxed time in a mountain village far from the bustle of the city soothes both mind and body.
quiz_en: If you stayed at a mountain village hot spring like Futakawa Onsen, what dishes would you hope for at dinner?

desc_en: This ocean park spreads along the Shirasaki coast in Yura. The contrast between the gleaming white limestone rocks and the clear blue sea is beautiful, earning the area comparisons to a famous European sea. From the observation deck you can take in the unique coastline of white rocks and the Kii Channel, and there is also a campground and diving spots. The white rocks dyed by the setting sun are also spectacular.
quiz_en: The Shirasaki coast, with its white limestone and blue sea, has been compared to which sea in Europe?

desc_en: This sea fishing park faces the calm Yura Bay in Yura. From well-built fishing platforms, even beginners and families can enjoy fishing with peace of mind. The bay is surrounded by green mountains, and the view of the gentle, quiet sea is soothing in itself. Various fish can be caught each season, and you can make the most of your time by the sea while leisurely dangling your line.
quiz_en: In the calm waters of the Yura Sea Fishing Park, which fish would you most like to try to catch?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) is located in the mountains of Minabe, known as the home of ume plums. Minabe is known as Japan's largest producer of ume and is also the birthplace of a premium variety that has become synonymous with high-quality umeboshi (pickled plums). In early spring the surrounding mountains are covered with white plum blossoms and wrapped in a sweet fragrance. After relaxing in the hot spring, try dishes made with local ume and umeboshi.
quiz_en: What is the leading ume plum variety that originated in Minabe Town, where Tsurunoyu Onsen is located?

desc_en: This historic temple in Hidakagawa is considered the oldest temple in Wakayama Prefecture. It is known as the setting of the legend of Anchin and Kiyohime, in which Kiyohime, spurned in love, transforms into a monstrous creature and burns Anchin to death as he hides inside the temple bell. In the grounds, monks tell the legend using picture scrolls in a practice called "etoki seppo," and in cherry-blossom season the approach and grounds are brightly colored.
quiz_en: In the legend of Dojo-ji, what creature did Kiyohime turn into out of the rage of her spurned love?

name_en: Sakinoyu and Seaside Baths of Nanki-Shirahama Onsen
desc_en: Shirahama Onsen, counted among Japan's three oldest hot springs, has Sakinoyu, an open-air bath set on rocks where the rough waves of the Pacific crash. It is a historic bath said to have been visited by emperors and nobles since the Man'yo era, and you can bathe while gazing at the vast ocean before you. Public bathhouses are dotted along the shore, so you can stroll to Shirarahama Beach while enjoying bathhouse hopping.
quiz_en: Shirahama Onsen, home of Sakinoyu, is counted along with Arima and Dogo as one of what group of hot springs?

desc_en: Located halfway up Mount Nachi, this is one of the Kumano Sanzan, the three grand shrines of Kumano, and is said to have begun with the worship of Nachi Falls as a deity. From the grounds lined with vermilion buildings you can see the Nachi mountains and the falls, and the view of the falls beside the three-story pagoda of neighboring Seiganto-ji is the quintessential Kumano scene. At the annual fire festival on July 14, giant torches purify the stone steps in a spectacular rite.
quiz_en: What is the name of the fire festival held every July at Kumano Nachi Taisha in which giant torches purify the stone steps?

desc_en: Plunging 133 meters from the primeval forest of Mount Nachi, this is one of Japan's most celebrated waterfalls. Its drop is said to be the highest of any single-tier waterfall in Japan, and it is counted among Japan's three great waterfalls. Since ancient times the falls themselves have been worshipped as a deity and serve as the sacred object of a shrine. Standing before the falls, amid the roar and the falling spray, you cannot help but feel awe toward nature.
quiz_en: What is the name of the shrine right in front of Nachi Falls that worships the waterfall itself as its sacred object?

desc_en: The sacred sites of Kumano, made up of the Kumano Sanzan (Kumano Hongu Taisha, Kumano Hayatama Taisha, and Kumano Nachi Taisha), together with Seiganto-ji on Mount Nachi, Fudarakusan-ji, and others, form the core of the World Heritage Site "Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range." Long a center of faith blending Shinto and Buddhism, Kumano drew everyone from retired emperors to commoners, who walked the Kumano Kodo to worship here in such numbers that the crowds were likened to a line of small creatures.
quiz_en: The endless lines of pilgrims heading to Kumano were compared to which small creature, giving rise to a famous phrase?

desc_en: This tuna-themed event is held at Katsuura Fishing Port in Nachikatsuura. Katsuura is known as one of Japan's leading ports for landing fresh tuna, and it prides itself on serving fresh, never-frozen tuna. On festival day, tuna-cutting shows and on-the-spot sales are held, drawing large crowds. Along with the energy of the port town, you can savor freshly caught flavors to your heart's content.
quiz_en: At the Katsuura Tuna Festival, which tuna dish would you most like to try, and how would you like it prepared?

desc_en: This castle-shaped observatory stands on a hill overlooking the Sendai River in Kawahara-cho, Tottori. Its keep-like exterior catches the eye, and from the top floor you can take in the flowing Sendai River, the townscape of Kawahara, and the mountains of Inaba. The surrounding area is a village of clear streams known for ayu (sweetfish) fishing, and with cherry blossoms in spring and autumn leaves in fall decorating the hill, you can enjoy views through all four seasons.
quiz_en: Which river fish, looked for in the Sendai River below the Kawahara Castle observatory, is popular with anglers in summer?

desc_en: Located in the heart of the city, within walking distance of Tottori Station, this is a rare urban onsen (hot spring) even by national standards. Since the spring was confirmed in the Meiji era, its waters have been enjoyed at inns, hotels, and public bathhouses around town. Its appeal is that you can casually take a dip after work or between sightseeing, and it is also a convenient base for visiting the Tottori Sand Dunes.
quiz_en: Using Tottori Onsen as a base, which famous Tottori attraction, known as one of Japan's largest sand dunes, would you visit?

desc_en: This is a quiet onsen (hot spring) resort in the mountains on the outskirts of Tottori City. It has a long history as a toji-ba, a place for therapeutic bathing, and its compact hot spring town is lined with inns and communal baths. A simple, old-fashioned atmosphere remains, and bathing alongside local people lets you feel the warmth of the Inaba countryside. It is close to the city, so you can easily make a trip here.
quiz_en: At a simple, traditional bathing retreat like Yoshioka Onsen, how would you like to spend an entire day from morning to night?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) wells up in the former castle town of Shikano Castle, which was ruled by the Sengoku warlord Kamei Korenori. Old-fashioned streets remain in the castle town, and you can stroll leisurely along its calm lanes. The moat of the castle ruins is known for its cherry blossoms, and in spring it bustles with blossom viewers. Warm up in the hot spring after a town walk to fully savor the charms of this small castle town in Inaba.
quiz_en: Who was the Sengoku warlord who ruled the castle town of Shikano Onsen and showed strong interest in overseas trade?

desc_en: This onsen (hot spring) wells up near Hamamura Beach in Ketaka-cho, facing the Sea of Japan. It is known as the birthplace of a Tottori folk song, and monuments related to the song can be seen around town. A short walk from the hot spring town brings you to a wide sandy beach where you can watch the sunset over the Sea of Japan. Seafood, such as Matsuba crab in winter and fresh fish and shellfish in summer, is another pleasure here.
quiz_en: What is the Tottori folk song, connected with scallop fishing, for which Hamamura Onsen is known as the birthplace?

desc_en: This forest park spreads across the mountains of eastern Tottori City. Walking trails and a campground have been laid out in the rich forest, letting you fully enjoy nature surrounded by trees. The forest changes its expression with the seasons, from the fresh greenery of spring and cool shade of summer to the autumn leaves. Forest bathing while listening to birdsong will refresh both mind and body.
quiz_en: If you went camping in the forest of Anzo Forest Park, what kind of camp meal would you like to cook?

desc_en: This summer festival is held in Hamamura, Ketaka-cho, the birthplace of the Tottori folk song "Kaigarabushi." During the festival, dancers dressed in matching yukata or happi coats dance through the town to the melancholy melody of Kaigarabushi. Savoring the lyrics that recall the hardships of scallop fishing in the past, you can enjoy a summer night in this seaside town together with the local people.
quiz_en: If you danced at the Kaigarabushi Festival, would you prefer to wear a yukata or a happi coat, and why?

desc_en: This summer festival is held in Aoya-cho, Tottori City, facing the Sea of Japan. Aoya is known for the Aoya Kamijichi site, the remains of a Yayoi-period settlement, and it also carries on a tradition of washi papermaking. On festival day, local people gather, and in the open atmosphere typical of a seaside town, you can spend a summer moment enjoying events and food stalls.
quiz_en: At the Aoya Yokoso Festival, what would you most like to see on a summer night in this seaside town?

desc_en: This shrine in Kokufu-cho, Tottori City, is the ichinomiya (highest-ranking shrine) of the old Inaba Province, and its official name is written with different characters. It is dedicated to Takenouchi no Sukune, known as a long-lived loyal retainer, and attracts worshippers seeking longevity and business prosperity. Because the shrine and Takenouchi no Sukune appeared on banknotes in the Meiji era, many visitors also come seeking blessings related to money.
quiz_en: Who is the ancient figure enshrined at Ube Shrine, known as a loyal retainer who lived a very long life?

desc_en: This Hachiman shrine stands in Baba, in the eastern part of central Tottori City. Wrapped in a sacred grove, its grounds are filled with a tranquility you would not expect in town, and it has been cherished as a center of faith for local people. Festivals are held throughout the year, and families can be seen visiting at milestones such as the New Year's first shrine visit and Shichi-Go-San, a celebration for children.
quiz_en: At a local shrine like Kurata Hachimangu, what special occasion do you remember visiting with your family?

desc_en: This shrine stands in Kuriya-cho, Tottori City. It is located in a quiet spot nestled against the mountains northeast of central Tottori, and a calm atmosphere flows through its tree-lined grounds. Although close to the town of Tottori, which developed as a castle town, it is a place where you can feel rich nature, and it is a fitting shrine to stop by for a quiet prayer during a walk.
quiz_en: If you visited the quiet grounds of Kurii Shrine, would you choose the season of fresh greenery or of autumn leaves?

desc_en: This shrine is associated with the myth of the "White Hare of Inaba" from the Kojiki and enshrines the white hare as a deity. In honor of the story of the white hare helped by a god, many worshippers come to pray for good relationships. The grounds contain Mitarashi Pond, where the white hare is said to have washed its wounds, and stone statues of white hares line the approach. The Sea of Japan spreads out right in front of the shrine.
quiz_en: In the myth of the White Hare of Inaba told at Hakuto Shrine, which god helped the injured white hare?

name_en: Tottori Deai no Mori Forest Park
desc_en: This forest park spreads across the hills of Katsurami in western Tottori City. Walking paths, an athletic course, and lawns have been laid out in the rich forest, so both children and adults can enjoy a full day in nature. It is close to Lake Koyama, and the colors of the flowers and trees change with each season. Just a short distance from the city center, it is a relaxing spot to enjoy forest bathing casually.
quiz_en: Deai no Mori means "forest of encounters." What flowers or creatures would you like to encounter there?

desc_en: This park in Yodoe-cho, Yonago, lets you experience ancient life and buildings. Yodoe is an area with many remaining burial mounds and ancient temple sites, and the park has reconstructions of ancient raised-floor storehouses and pit dwellings. From its spacious grounds you can see the majestic Mount Daisen, and amid scenery that ancient people may also have gazed upon, you can reflect on history.
quiz_en: Which highest peak of the Chugoku region, also called "Hoki Fuji," can be seen from Hoki Kodai no Oka Park?

desc_en: This park in Hikona, Yonago, facing Lake Nakaumi, is dedicated to observing waterbirds. In winter, tundra swans fly in from the direction of Siberia, and you can watch them swimming gracefully on the pond. Many other wild birds, including ducks and herons, also gather here, and you can observe them up close through telescopes from the large windows of the nature center.
quiz_en: Which large white migratory bird flies to Yonago Waterbird Sanctuary in winter and is popular for its graceful appearance?

desc_en: Facing the coast of Yumigahama, this is one of the leading onsen (hot spring) resorts of the San'in region. It is said to have begun when a hot spring bubbling up from the sea was discovered in the Meiji era, and its salty water has a reputation for warming the body well. It is also known as the Japanese birthplace of a multi-sport race. Inns and hotels line the shore, offering sunsets over the Sea of Japan and views of distant Mount Daisen.
quiz_en: Kaike Onsen is the Japanese birthplace of which sport that combines swimming, cycling, and running?
